translations.text: In days of old the people of Israel were enlightened and taught through Moses, the famous teacher, as the Lord of life, the high King of the heavens,
here in life, through his own word, set him over the people as a counsel for men, and himself told him the meaning of the mysteries, how he should teach the true way to the beloved people.
Then the leader of the people followed the teachings of the high King of the heavens, and the men did likewise, as they had been taught among the people;

if they began wavering deeds, the God of victories sent them harm from heaven as a reward for it, and at once they longed for peace from him, and quickly found it there, if they would let their sins be cast away.
Many are the virtues which that famous nation kept and practised in that host, while they were willing to love the Lord of life;

but their end was wretched and grievous, when they betrayed the Lord himself, set him on the cross and condemned him to the grave; he was hidden there, and on the third day he was shown to the peoples.

We have heard many men proclaim and write in letters that they kept four fasts and then offered a spotless beast, that is, a lamb or a young bullock, as a token of the Beloved One who before the world was free of stains.

But the Ruler of the kingdom arose from the tomb, filled with glories, and with the dwellers of heaven sought his home, a dwelling among the angels, and promises that hope to us all, if with a right mind we will follow his counsels.
No one filled with foulness, stained with sin, comes in there; rather, he shall depart to his doom.
Now we must praise here in this life the precious Author of deeds, and fulfil for him the count of the years with our almsdeeds and with fasts, as the wise Moses once declared,
and we must steadfastly keep those appointed times among the English, as the man in Rome, Gregory, pope of men, set them down for us.
We must keep the first fast in the first week of Lent, in the month that throughout the realm of the Romans is called March,
and there, in bright order, twelve lessons of the mysteries shall be read in the hall of the mighty one, the high King of the heavens, to praise him with song and honour the glorious Giver of glory.

After Eastertide another fast is to be celebrated by the peoples of the Britons with like praise, which is appointed for the week that comes after the Sunday which priests throughout the wide world call the day of Pentecost, in the month, as it seems to me, that has from of old been called June.

Then the third fast on earth for the children of men is, in every respect with like ordering, to be celebrated in the precious hall with bright song in the week that comes before the day of the equinox for the sons of men, in the month, as I have heard, that is called September.
We must keep the fourth fast in the week that comes just before the Lord's birth,

and with earnest words and deeds, at that same time and with all mindfulness, we must glorify the King of glory, the Prince, in every respect, just as before, and pray the gracious, beloved Lord of peoples for life.
In these fasts the fourth day and the sixth, together with the seventh, are to be kept for the Lord of life and celebrated with the mysteries of the books at about the ninth hour;
there is no one on earth, unless sickness alone constrains him, who may consume [?] anything hot or wet before then, as the public judgment of the books decrees for us.
If, then, the lords of the Franks who have come from the south tell you that here on earth you must keep any of the commands that Moses once spoke to the people,
Never become an accepter of that; rather, hold to that same thing which came to you from the south from the shepherd of the realm of the Romans, Gregory, pope of men.
thus he himself, the teacher of the people, established and ordained the services, the times of fasting; we still now follow them devoutly throughout England.
As he himself decreed at that see, the priests of Saint Peter afterwards taught that same thing for a long lifetime, so that you must never follow others.
We also keep a fast of forty days before the resurrection of our Lord, which people now call Lent. The good man, the famous Moses, first began it before he climbed the mountain;
he kept that fast for forty days and nights together, so that he tasted nothing before he received the precious law of the Lord.

There the Lord himself gave him the glorious craft of books, wrapped in fire, written by his own holy hand, and commanded him to teach and show it to the people with the skill of men [?], as a sign to all.
so that through fasting we may win peace and the deep mysteries of the Lord, which every people ought to learn, if the Lord grants us any of that excellence.
Again Elijah, the famous man, took food in the wilderness, where one of the Lord's angels set feast-bread before him together with water,
and he was strengthened by that sturdy food to fast forty days and nights together, so that he ate nothing before he, the holy one, went to Mount Horeb.
Let us rightly consider that mystery: the famous servant did not have the strength to climb step by step to the height before that feast was given to him by the angel.
We are in the wilderness, without the bliss of glory, in a desolation empty of all joys; now is the time for help, holy Lord, to show how we may climb your glorious mountain.
Those who teach the Lord's word by their deeds are counted as angels to the dwellers on earth.

Let us eagerly partake of that sustenance and the precious food, the Lord's teaching; let us fast from sinful deeds in this way, in abstinence here in this life, so that we may climb in strength the mountain of glories, as the old Elijah once did.
We should consider how the holy one departed from this earthly place to visit glory: fire clothed him, and four splendid, proud steeds carried him away to paradise,
There Christ the Savior has promised us a home in bliss, if here we keep that fast from sins and seek the heavenly homeland.
Now at last our Saviour Christ, the holy guardian of heaven, helped and taught us.

Free of sins, he let himself be dipped in a precious washing, the bath of baptism, and, guilty of nothing, he put away food for forty days and as many nights, as a lesson to people that in Lent they should keep a fast of exactly forty days.

There in the desolate place Christ's adversary, old and wicked, tempted him. He saw the glorious Lord in the likeness of men, and then, mindful of sin, he began to hope that he could fix his arrows in that body;
but there was none of those sins in him, and the dispenser of harm withdrew, and angels came there to their Lord.

Sinful-minded man, if the guardian of torments dares to tempt you, as he did Christ, the glorious Lord of hosts, who was without sins, he cannot shoot anything into you if he does not find a mark of wickedness at the [?].
but he slinks backward, and the holy, virtuous angels help you everywhere, if here you follow the Lord in your deeds.

We have now set out how the famous men of old kept a fast of forty days, and through God's man we command that every person who lives on earth keep a fast of exactly forty days before the resurrection of our Lord, until the ninth hour,
and that he partake of neither flesh nor sins, lest he be guilty.
Priests must sing mass and pray to the Lord daily during the fast that he be a friend to the people throughout the earth,
And they must tell each of their sins to the priests and atone for their secret deeds by deeds of word and work, and fully appease the Lord of glory through almsgiving.
So there is great need for many peoples that the priests themselves do not sin and do not lie too deeply sunk in their vices.
Who can plead with his lord against any punishment if he has previously angered him bitterly, makes no amends for it, and instead renews the offence of the old quarrel by his deeds every day?
If the priest does not know how to keep himself in virtue through fear of the Lord, then, man of the people, pay no heed to the sins that the consecrated man commits here,

but with right understanding you must gladly carry out the teaching that he gives you as counsel. Let him drink for himself the muddy water or the day-clear water from the road: that is the teaching of glory.
But I can tell, burdened with sorrows, how the priests renew strife, anger the Lord daily, and with malice lead astray every one of the people who wishes to follow them;
straight away in the morning they sing mass, and, exhausted [?], driven by thirst, they go through the streets after the tapster.
Lo! They begin to lie falsely and repeatedly urge the tapster on, saying that he may without sin give them oysters to eat and fine wine around morning time,
so that it seems to me that the dog and the wolf behave the same way in the world, and do not consider whom they seize for food, lacking all moderation.

Then, sitting, they begin to fill themselves; they [?] sin; they hand out drink again and again; they tell every man, with God's leave [?], that anyone may, when weary, take a drink of wine after he has had mass, and also eat oysters and other fish from the sea
